> Likewise, setting `absorbent` and `rough` based on the value being negative is unintuitive. In terms of discoverability, it's better to have separate methods that show up in autocompletion.

Note that this is already the case (albeit undocumented) for the body-wide friction and bounce, where `rough` and `absorbent` are represented as negative values, so this is not new to this PR. I would personally prefer to see that the two are generally consistent in how they're set, even if the body-wide values are technically set through `body_set_param`, and not some `body_set_friction`.

Formally adding `rough` and `absorbent` to the physics server API would also further cement what is arguably a bit of a quirk in Godot, and might complicate efforts such as godotengine/godot-proposals#11715 that aims to add different ways of combining friction and bounce values.

I do agree that the `NAN` default values looks somewhat off though, but I haven't had time yet to look much deeper than that.

I'll try to find some time this week to do another pass on this.

> We can't change what's exposed once it lands in a stable release, so we need to make sure it's rock-solid.

I will say that I am leaning towards suggesting that we do go with this API for `PhysicsServer*D` after all:

```gdscript
body_set_shape_friction_override(body: RID, shape_idx: int, friction: float) -> void
body_set_shape_bounce_override(body: RID, shape_idx: int, bounce: float) -> void

body_get_shape_friction_override(body: RID, shape_idx: int) -> float
body_get_shape_bounce_override(body: RID, shape_idx: int) -> float

body_set_enable_shape_friction_override(body: RID, shape_idx: int, enable: bool) -> void
body_set_enable_shape_bounce_override(body: RID, shape_idx: int, enable: bool) -> void

body_is_shape_friction_override_enabled(body: RID, shape_idx: int) -> bool
body_is_shape_bounce_override_enabled(body: RID, shape_idx: int) -> bool
```

However, what I'm still unsure of is whether or not we would mandate that enabling/disabling should be completely disconnected from the value itself or not, where the value would persist even after disabling.

If the value must in fact persist even after disabling, then that of course changes how we need to store things, but we could also just document that:

1. Setting the value implicitly enables the override.
2. Disabling the override effectively resets the value.

... which would let implementers (i.e. our physics servers and any third-party extensions) omit any sort of bool/bit/flag for the enabled state, but I'm not sure if we're just trading in one awkward API for another in that case.

Also, if all we're doing is trying to do is save on memory from this enabled bool/bit/flag, then why are we going with the "dense" storage (e.g. `LocalVector<float>`) for these material values in the first place? Wouldn't the more common use-case of per-shape materials be that you rely on the body's material for the majority of the shapes, and then selectively set a few shapes to override that material? If so, then you would ideally store this in some kind of "sparse" storage anyway, like a shape-index-to-material-value map, ~~at which point the enabled state comes "for free" by virtue of the shape index' presence in this map~~[^1].

If you'll allow me to generalize even more, the vast majority of bodies created will likely not use these overrides, and if they do, they will likely consist of only a handful of shapes, at which point the cost/benefit analysis of dense vs sparse storage is likely moot anyway.

So maybe we do in fact keep the material values separate from their enabled state, and thus end up with what I would argue is a (mostly) better API?

[^1]: EDIT: I realized the moment I posted this that you would of course need to have the enabled state separate even with sparse storage, since disabling would otherwise reset the value, but my points still stand I guess.

As another last-minute decision, I've omitted the `body_is_shape_(friction|bounce)_overridden` physics server methods from the API that I suggested above, because I struggle to see a use-case for such a query, and it's not something that's needed by the scene nodes anyway.

If anyone needs this in the future it can trivially be added then instead.

So the `PhysicsServer*D` API would look like this instead, which I'm mostly happy with:

```gdscript
func body_set_shape_friction_override(body: RID, shape_idx: int, friction: float) -> void
func body_clear_shape_friction_override(body: RID, shape_idx: int) -> void
func body_get_shape_friction(body: RID, shape_idx: int) -> float
```

Does this have any chance of working with Heightmap Shapes? (I belive these construct a grid of Quad shapes under the hood, that are tested for in a specific way due to the nature of heightmaps.)

In Terrain3D I would like to be able to send a physics material "ID" for each Quad. Since We have access to an index map that could determine the dominant texture for any given quad, and that texture has other properties associated with it already, linking each texture ID (upto 32) to a physics material, would essentially Let us have paintable physics materials.
